author: Jocelyn Flores
title: Measles cases rise to 15 in New Mexico detention centers - NewsBreak
text:
By Jocelyn Flores ,
1 hours ago
EL PASO, Texas ( KTSM ) — The New Mexico Department of Health confirmed the measles case count to 15, linked to three county detention centers.
Ten cases are in the Luna County Detention Center, three in the Doña Ana County Detention Center and two in the Hidalgo County Detention Center. All cases involve federal detainees, according to NMDOH.
NM says measles cases now at 13, including 3 at Doña Ana County jail The department said they have sent vaccination crews to all facilities to reduce the risk of spreading.
“Measles is very contagious and there have been almost 1500 measles infections reported this year in the United States. The best way to prevent measles infection is to be fully vaccinated,” Dr. Chad Smelser, medical epidemiologist with NMDOH, said.
Measles symptoms can develop between seven and 21 days after exposure. Symptoms begin with fever, cough, runny nose and red eyes, followed by a red-spotted rash that usually starts on the head or face and spreads down the body.
Health officials say that people can pass measles to someone else from four days before to four days after the rash first appears.
The NMDOH encourages residents to review their vaccination records, including for measles, as the travel season continues and can lead to additional risks, particularly if traveling out of the state or country.
Earlier this month, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention praised the NMDOH for its public messaging and vaccination strategies during the 2025 measles outbreak. Over 60,000 people got their MMR shots at the time, a 55 percent increase over the same period the previous year.
You can call your doctor or emergency department if you have symptoms and believe you were possibly exposed to measles, so health providers can plan for your visit and minimize exposure. Health officials say don’t walk in.
Those who are unsure about their vaccination status can access shot records at the NMDOH’s website or through the department’s helpline at 1-833-SWNURSE (1-833-796-8773) for guidance in English or Spanish. Residents can also text questions to 66364.
For more information, you can visit NMHealth.org in English or Spanish .
